note: Small Gasconade River access at the end of a gravel road, with a gravel camping loop of pull-in pads, a privy and a concrete boat ramp. Despite the name it is on the mainland bank, reached by road. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'Boat ramp and individual campsites' / 'Camping: Individual Campsites', Rule 140 standard; map 8 'Primitive Camping' symbols on an MDC gravel loop with gravel pull-in pads (imagery). Road access, not an island. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights manual + 2027 permit; privy added; 8 sites. Pin on a pad - fine. Not waterfront kept (river ~70-90 m through woods and the ramp lot). Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: page 'Boat ramp and individual campsites', Things to Do 'Camping: Individual Campsites', Rule 140 standard (no permit rule). Map (6/16/2021): eight 'Primitive Camping' symbols around a gravel loop ('MDC Unimproved Road') with a privy and parking. Imagery: four-plus gravel pull-in pads on the west end of the loop, 15-20 m long - a 23-ft rig fits. Two points (86, 87) sit in woods at the east end beside the ramp lot.

ISLAND: not an island in practice - the map shows Helds Island Rd (county road) running to the area on the west bank of the Gasconade; page directions 'Route K north 4 miles until it turns into a gravel road, continue 2 miles to the Access entrance'. No ford or crossing.

WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept): pads are 80-150 m from the river through a wooded bank; the east-end points 86/87 are ~70 m from the water with the ramp lot and a wooded bank between. No open apron.
PIN: 38.55264,-91.59974 = GIS 515, on a pull-in pad of the loop - fine.
CLUSTERS: one loop, no split; near.py nothing else within 3 km.
Season (manual, year-round) left as stored. Riverside low ground - floods possible but none posted.

FEES FROM MARCH 2027 (applies to every MDC area entry and the state:missouri-conservation-areas policy row): MDC release https://mdc.mo.gov/node/307038 ('Campers will need permits to camp on MDC areas starting in March'): 'The Missouri Conservation Commission gave final approval at its Oct. 23 open meeting ... to regulation changes ... that would require campers to purchase a permit to camp on MDC areas starting in March 2027'; 'purchase a permit for $5 for up to five days of camping on conservation areas for up to 10 people'; 'Each person will be limited to three consecutive camping permits and six camping permits annually'; 'available for purchase beginning in March online, at a permit vendor, or over the phone'. The camping page still says 'All camping on conservation areas is free' (true until then), so nightly_low/high 0 written as today's value with the 2027 permit in fees.note; the policy row's fees and booking note need the same update.
Note rewritten: acreage, generic MDC text, the 14-day limit (now booking.max_stay_nights), 'site length not published' and directions dropped.
